candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care client-needs subcategory (15–21% of items); includes referrals, continuity of care, client education, and coordination of community resources.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Referral to evidence-based self-management and psychosocial resources
candidate.educational_objective: Connect clients with epilepsy to evidence-based self-management and support resources that build coping and disease-management skills while continuing prescribed medical care and follow-up.

options.A: An epilepsy self-management program or support resource that teaches coping, decision-making, and skills for living with epilepsy
options.B: A peer or self-management program used instead of prescribed antiseizure medication and clinical follow-up
options.C: No additional support, because stress, isolation, and self-management difficulties are not recognized concerns in epilepsy
options.D: A program only if seizures are uncontrolled, because self-management resources have no role for other people with epilepsy

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current CDC epilepsy guidance states that self-management programs can help people learn skills and strategies to make good health decisions and feel better while living with epilepsy. CDC-funded programs address challenges including stress, stigma, isolation, mental health, treatment management, and use of available resources; some programs are available through group, telephone, or online formats. These resources complement—not replace—prescribed treatment and professional follow-up. B incorrectly substitutes supportive care for medical treatment. C denies problems explicitly recognized by CDC. D adds an unsupported severity restriction.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports referral to epilepsy self-management resources for coping, health decision-making, psychosocial challenges, and day-to-day disease management as an adjunct to ongoing professional care.
candidate.source_document_title: Managing Epilepsy; Managing Epilepsy Well Network

CDC 'Managing Epilepsy Well Network' → Overview: self-management programs develop strategies and skills for medication/appointment management, provider communication, stress and mental-health challenges, stigma, fatigue, and finding resources.
